title: Salsiccia e Fagioli alla Toscana
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A simple, hearty Tuscan pairing of grilled or pan-seared sausage with cannellini beans stewed in tomato and sage, a reliable trattoria staple found throughout the region.
longDesc: This dish embodies Tuscan simplicity at its best, needing little more than good sausage and beans, the sage-scented tomato sauce doing most of the work to bring the two together into a genuinely satisfying meal.
ingredients: 400 g (2 cups) dried cannellini beans, soaked overnight (or 2 cans, drained)
80 ml (⅓ cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: If using dried beans, simmer the soaked beans in fresh water until tender, about 1 hour, then drain.
Warm half the olive oil in a large pot and sauté the garlic and sage until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes and cooked beans, and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil in a skillet and cook the sausages until browned and cooked through, about 15–18 minutes.
Serve the sausages alongside a generous portion of the beans.
chefTips: Cook the garlic gently in the oil to avoid bitterness, which would compound with the beans' mild flavor.
Good-quality, well-seasoned sausage makes a real difference in this simple dish.
This is an excellent make-ahead dish, as the beans improve with a little resting time.
commonMistakes: Burning the garlic while infusing the oil, which turns the whole dish bitter.
Overcooking the beans until they turn mushy rather than staying intact.
Using bland sausage, which is a primary flavor component of this simple pairing.
storage: The beans keep refrigerated for up to 4 days.
healthBenefits: Cannellini beans provide plant-based protein and fiber.
culturalNote: Salsiccia e fagioli is a reliable, beloved staple across Tuscan trattorie, exemplifying the region's confidence in simple, well-executed combinations.
